title: Every write on one partition
question: A DynamoDB table of click events is throttled at a fraction of its provisioned capacity. Metrics show almost all writes landing on one partition. What is wrong with the design?
context: The partition key is the event date, such as 2026-09-24, and the sort key is a timestamp. Every event written today shares the same partition key.

options.label: Provisioned capacity is too low; raise it until the throttling stops
options.why: Capacity is spread across partitions, and a single partition has its own limit. Doubling the table's capacity barely raises what one key can take, so most of what you pay for stays unused.

options.label: The key has one hot value a day; spread it with a high-cardinality key
options.why: A partition key should spread load, not group it. Keying by something with many values — the user or device id — or adding a suffix to the date and querying the suffixes in parallel, lets writes use every partition instead of one.

options.label: DynamoDB cannot take this write rate; move the events to PostgreSQL
options.why: It takes far higher write rates when they are spread across keys. The limit being hit is the design's, and a relational database would need the same thought about hot rows and indexes.

options.label: Put a Redis cache in front of the table to absorb the incoming writes
options.why: A cache helps with repeated reads. These are unique writes that must be stored; putting a cache in front only moves the throttling or turns it into write-behind with its own risk of losing events.
